chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Ibn Abi Hamzah, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, who said:

I asked him about salat in a ship, and he said: He should perform salat while sitting if he is not able to stand in the ship. And he should not perform salat in the ship while he is able to reach the shore. And he said: He performs salat in the ship and turns his face toward the qiblah, then performs salat however it turns.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship or vessel in which the prayer is being performed
key_terms.الشَّطِّ: the shore, meaning dry land accessible for prayer
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) being discussed in the context of travel by ship
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the direction of prayer toward which one turns the face
key_terms.جَالِسٌ: sitting, when standing is not possible

ai.seo_question: How should salat be performed in a ship according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on performing salat in a ship. It states that one may pray sitting if standing is not possible, that prayer in the ship should be avoided when one can pray on shore, and that one should begin facing the qiblah and then continue even as the ship turns.
